final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition with a CHF 100 billion SNB liquidity facility and explicit creditor waterfall documentation, to be announced Sunday evening before Monday market open. SNB executed a CHF 20 billion emergency draw Friday night as a confidence signal, with Federal Council committing to transparent public disclosure of the loss-absorption cap and creditor hierarchy.
minority_objections: FINMA initially resisted explicit public disclosure of AT1 and creditor waterfall, preferring sealed documentation to preserve legal defensibility
Wealth client and AT1 rep repeatedly warned that implicit language would trigger Monday withdrawals and litigation regardless of sealed documentation
key_conflicts: Transparency vs legal defensibility: whether to name AT1 protection and creditor hierarchy in Sunday's public statement or keep it sealed in acquisition docs
Operational ceiling vs political floor: whether the 100 billion cap is a hard limit SNB will not breach or a flexible buffer that invites resolution signaling if exceeded
Timeline compression: multiple parties demanding binding commitments, legal certifications, and board approvals by 10 p.m. Friday—operationally infeasible
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to explicit public disclosure of the 100 billion cap and creditor waterfall in Sunday's statement, abandoning the sealed-documentation approach
SNB committed to a hard 100 billion ceiling with no operational breach, accepting that deposit flight beyond that triggers documented creditor haircuts
UBS agreed to sign binding acquisition agreement by 10 p.m. Friday contingent on FINMA legal certification of the waterfall
FINMA agreed to issue written legal certification of the creditor waterfall by 9 p.m. Friday to enable UBS board approval
red_lines: SNB: 100 billion CHF absolute ceiling on public-sector exposure—no breach under any scenario
Federal Council: creditor and AT1 losses above 100 billion must be documented and enforceable to hold political line with Parliament
UBS: acquisition agreement must be binding with explicit loss-absorption waterfall before Monday open or UBS will not execute
Wealth client and AT1 rep: explicit public protection language required in Sunday statement or clients withdraw before Monday open
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Operational feasibility of the Friday-night timeline: legal certifications, board approvals, and acquisition agreement finalization by 10 p.m. were demanded but never confirmed as achievable
Mid-week breach scenarios: if 30-40 billion is drawn in 48 hours and haircuts fall below 15%, the room never locked whether SNB stays silent or announces drawdown—leaving confidence risk unresolved
Litigation timing: AT1 rep warned that lawsuits would begin Monday morning regardless of documentation, but no mitigation strategy was proposed beyond transparency
downstream_risk_variables: Monday deposit flight velocity: if withdrawals exceed 30-40 billion in 48 hours, collateral floor and asset-sale velocity may force SNB below stated haircut tolerance
AT1 litigation risk: even with explicit waterfall documentation, AT1 holders may sue to challenge hierarchy inversion or loss allocation
Parliamentary backlash: Federal Council's 100 billion cap may face political challenge if losses approach that ceiling mid-week and require public explanation
UBS board approval: acquisition agreement signature by 10 p.m. Friday was demanded but never confirmed as executed
uncertainty_notes: The room ended without confirming that the 10 p.m. Friday deadline for legal certification, board approvals, and acquisition agreement signature was actually met. The operational mechanics for handling 30-40 billion draws in 48 hours—specifically whether SNB announces drawdowns or stays silent—remained unresolved. The creditor waterfall documentation was agreed in principle but not finalized in writing before the meeting terminated.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: UBS CEO stated 'a liquidity facility doesn't move my needle' and demanded loss protection guarantees; Federal Council asked 'what's the actual rescue option' beyond SNB liquidity, driving the shift to acquisition structure
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: The entire rescue architecture converged on UBS acquisition with binding agreement by 10 p.m. Friday; Federal Council locked 'acquisition effective immediately' as the Sunday announcement centerpiece
marker_evidence.government_support: The 100 billion SNB facility and Federal Council loss-absorption cap became binding constraints on the deal structure; SNB executed 20 billion draw unilaterally as government backstop
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client issued 6 a.m. Sunday ultimatum threatening withdrawal; multiple parties cited 30-40 billion deposit flight in 48 hours as the stress scenario driving operational design
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 rep demanded explicit protection language in Sunday statement and threatened litigation if waterfall remained sealed; Federal Council confirmed 'AT1 and equity take documented losses beyond 100 billion'
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Discussed extensively (AT1 vs creditor vs equity hierarchy, who absorbs losses above 100B) but did not force a binding concession—Federal Council stated waterfall would be documented but kept implicit in public statement initially
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep warned 'litigation the moment the deal closes' and 'AT1 holders sue Monday morning'; acknowledged as inevitable but did not change the decision to proceed with transparent waterfall documentation
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: FINMA demanded statutory authority 'in the next 30 minutes'; multiple parties set 10 p.m. Friday deadlines for legal certification, board approvals, and acquisition signature—these deadlines drove the entire decision sequence
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Raised repeatedly ('Monday morning depositors don't care about statutory authority,' 'Monday run,' 'market panic at Monday open') but did not materially alter the decision—the room was already designing for Monday confidence, so this was context not constraint
